decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line with several models in the firm's main category, it would normally stay unless sales or margin performance clearly underperform expectations.
The comfort insole still fits the footwear ecosystem, but as a more easily substitutable accessory it remains a plausible candidate for range simplification against the firm's other insole offers.
The supportive insole supports cross-selling and functional differentiation for work footwear, though some consolidation risk remains because the firm now has multiple insole variants.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series with its own dedicated presentation looks strategically important in the firm's core business and is unlikely to be withdrawn absent clear market disappointment.

Firefighter and rescue boots serve a specialized niche but are closely aligned with the firm's protective-footwear expertise, so management would usually continue the line while building presence in that segment.
Because the moulded insole was highlighted as a flagship direction, the firm would be very reluctant to remove it and would more likely build around it than discontinue it.
